summary: On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), which aligns a student model's token-level distribution with that of its self-teacher prompted by privileged context, has emerged as a promising direction to mitigate reward sparsity in sequence-level post-training paradigms. However, OPSD often fails to achieve continuous performance gains during training.
takeaways: In this paper, we find that the model's limited self-teaching capability underlies this phenomenon by generating unreliable guidance on certain samples.
First, using these rewards as training objectives, we perform teacher-oriented optimization to continuously enhance the model's self-teaching capability during distillation.
However, OPSD often fails to achieve continuous performance gains during training.
